newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CKI in 1,000 MW of China power projects.
newsitem.headline: CKI in 1,000 MW of China power projects.

text.p: Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd (CKI) on Sunday said it has signed agreements or letters of intent for power projects in China with total capacity of more than 1,000 megawatts (MW).

"As of now, we are negotiating projects in Liaoning, Hebei, Henan and Guangdong, for a total capacity of over 2,000 MW, of which we have already signed agreements and letters of intent for over 1,000 MW," said H.L. Kam, managing director of CKI.
The company also confirmed it had recently signed three agreements to develop heat and electricity co-generation power plants in Fushun city in Liaoning province.
"These Fushun city power agreements are amongst the many agreements and letters of intent signed in the past few months pertaining to power," Kam said in a company statement.

CKI said it plans to invest 450 million yuan in the 740 million yuan project, which will have a joint venture period of 20 years. The plants have a combined installed capacity of 170 MW of electricity from two Chinese and one European generators.
The plants will also supply heat for local use in the forms of high and low pressure steam for industries and residences.
Some 38 percent of the plants' revenues will come from heat, and 62 percent from electricity. -- HK Newsroom (852) 2843-6441
